Status: LIVING - exact implementation state and next task only.

## Current phase

Noon Curveball adaptation is implemented and awaiting approved verification in the official Entire mirror clone.

## Completed

- Cloned `ChetanReddyC/cli` through the Entire mirror in the India region.
- Enabled Entire project tracking and installed Codex hooks in the clone.
- IMPLEMENTED / UNVERIFIED: Task 1 React/Vite + Express/TypeScript bootstrap.
- Added one-command development scripts, shared Zod bootstrap contracts, environment configuration, repository-context resolution, thin API/runtime files, and the initial responsive dashboard shell.
- Installed locked npm dependencies and generated `package-lock.json`.
- Installed Entire Graph v0.4.0, initialized its repository agent guide, and ran the required pre-change search and impact analysis.
- IMPLEMENTED / UNVERIFIED: sensitive-repository privacy boundary across Checkpoint ingestion, canonical contracts, deterministic local review/handoff, API, and React presentation.
- Raw transcript bytes remain inside the local Entire adapter and are never included in the external evidence projection. Prompt and transcript evidence are marked local-only.
- Incomplete context is schema-enforced as provisional with no Intent Guard score; the UI labels complete, incomplete, and not-assessed states separately.
- Added a deterministic redacted/missing Checkpoint fixture and focused privacy-boundary tests.
- IMPLEMENTED / UNVERIFIED: Task 3 canonical evidence provenance and privacy-safe retrieval boundary.
- Evidence now carries deterministic IDs, content hashes, and Entire Checkpoint provenance.
- Added a narrow Databricks AI Search adapter with Delta Sync trigger, metadata-only query construction, canonical hit validation, and explicit local fallback.
- Added live `CONTEXT.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, and `RISKS.md` repository records for the Curveball architecture and remaining risks.

## Verification status

Not run. The Curveball slice is IMPLEMENTED / UNVERIFIED; verification requires explicit user approval under the Buildathon execution contract.

## Next task

Implement Section 16 Task 4: the on-demand semantic Review Engine, deterministic Intent Guard scoring for complete context, evidence-reference validation, and filesystem `ReviewStore` caching. Preserve the local provisional path for incomplete context and do not send raw prompts or transcripts to the analysis provider.

## Current blockers and constraints

- The supplied attachment was not present in the workspace, so the implementation uses a representative redacted/missing Checkpoint fixture pending replacement with the official fixture if its shape differs.
- Final semantic diff and runtime verification remain blocked on the approval-first verification gate.

item.stdout:
Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)

Usage:
  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]

Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with source and file:line inline, budgeted to drop straight into context. This is the first move for almost every locate task.

By default search returns: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as full function bodies), RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus other tests over the same code (ALSO COVERING), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the concept is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC), a VERIFY line (the narrowest test command for the file), and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a switch over a sealed set would fail at runtime. The three reference blocks (container map, signature types, declaration card) are OFF by default because they cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all turns them on for interactive reading.

--top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every eligible file).

Ranking returns one region per unit, which is right for code and wrong for whole prose documents: one markdown document can hold the answer across several distant regions. So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). Separately, and on prose of any shape including headed documents, when fewer distinct units match than --top-k asked for, the spare slots are spent returning finer regions of the same document as results of their own (multi-resolution retrieval) — strictly additive, so it never displaces a unit and never breaches --max-context-bytes. --single-resolution turns that off. The two stack: a headed document can be ranked by section AND have spare slots filled with promoted passages, so a prose payload may carry both.

Flags:
  --query <text>            The task or bug in one plain sentence (required)
  --repo <path>             Repository to search (default: current repo)
  --top-k <n>               Number of results to return (default: 10)
  --format text|json|ndjson|agent
                            Output format; text is tiered for reading, agent is compact (default: json)
  --head                    Search the committed tree (cached) instead of the working tree
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth; use full for bug-fix/locate (call-graph active) (default: fast)
  --deep                    Also run the exhaustive BM25 pass and fuse it (slower)
  --single-resolution       One result per ranked unit; do not spend spare slots on finer regions of a prose document
  --document-resolution     Rank a prose document as one unit; do not rank its sections separately
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Output byte budget; 0 = unbounded (default: 24576)
  --reference-blocks all|container-map,signature-types,type-card
                            Turn reference blocks back on (off by default)
  --max-indexed-files <n>   Bound cold-search parsing to N files
  --index-all-files         Widen cold-search parsing to every file
  --cache-dir <path>        Override the committed-tree cache directory
  --no-cache                Disable the committed-tree cache

Examples:
  entire graph search --repo . --query "token refresh returns 401" --format text --top-k 8
  entire graph search --repo . --query "csv export ordering" --profile full

Usage:
  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]

So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). # OpenAI Docs

Provide current, cited OpenAI product, API, model, and Codex guidance. Read zero or one primary reference.

**First substantive action:** Search the user's exact requested official OpenAI documentation topic and any explicitly named model using a concise, topic-specific query of 2-6 essential terms. A specific Codex feature, setting, command, error, model, or requested citation remains docs-first. Mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons are official documentation questions, not manual-first Codex requests.

For generic software tasks, answer the software task directly. OpenAI implementation, debugging, SDK, API, prompting, agent, and eval requests are not generic.

For a straightforward factual or citation-only request, follow the source order and do not read a route reference. This includes straightforward API facts, ChatGPT Work or mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons, model tiers, aliases, Pro mode, reasoning settings, factual migration baselines, and narrow Codex facts. ## Choose one primary route

Use the first matching route, and read its reference only when the requested task needs that specialized workflow:

- **Explicitly requested local documentation integration:** Read [integration guidance](references/mcp-diagnostics.md) only when the user explicitly requests that local integration.

- **Product, API, ChatGPT Work, and mixed Chat/Work/Codex documentation:** Read [official-docs.md](references/official-docs.md) only when fetched official pages leave source selection, API schemas, or the requested implementation unresolved. This route is not manual-first.
- **Explicitly broad Codex setup, orientation, or cross-topic synthesis:** Read [codex-self-knowledge.md](references/codex-self-knowledge.md) when the eligible Codex manual or deeper Codex procedures are needed.

## Webhook Verification

Verifying webhook signatures is optional but encouraged.

For more information about webhooks, see the API docs.

### Parsing webhook payloads

For most use cases, you will likely want to verify the webhook and parse the payload at the same time. Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in settings. Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

Usage:
  entire session attach <session-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -a, --agent string     Agent that created the session (see 'entire agent list' for registered agents, including external) (default "claude-code")
  -f, --force            Skip confirmation and amend the last commit with the checkpoint trailer (best-effort; if the amend fails the checkpoint is still created and the trailer is printed for manual paste)
  -h, --help             help for attach
      --review           Tag the attached session as an agent review
      --skills strings   Optional: declare which review skills were run in this session. Only used with --review

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
